explanations: leaseExpiresAt is computed from Date.now() after tryAcquire resolves. The store started the TTL when it processed the request, so time spent on the response path (a slow network, GC pause, or event-loop stall) is silently added to the local view of the lease. If that delay exceeds safetyMarginMs, this node believes it is leader after the store has already expired the lease and another node may hold it. The start time should be captured before sending the request and the expiry computed from that. The fencing token in settle() limits the damage, but the local leadership check is still wrong.

The catch block only logs; leaseExpiresAt is untouched, so isLeader() keeps returning true until the old expiry minus safetyMarginMs. The setTimeout after the try/catch still schedules the next tick. Only a successful but non-acquired response resets leaseExpiresAt, and the error is caught so there is no unhandled rejection.

settle() takes the fencing token, and its result type includes stale_token and already_settled, so the ledger is the final arbiter. isLeader() is a local check that both nodes can pass; nothing shown makes pendingBatches exclusive; the scheduler keeps no cache of settled ids.

It requires renewEveryMs to be below leaseMs - safetyMarginMs, the window in which isLeader() returns true, so renewal happens before the node would consider itself expired. Exclusivity is the store's job, the check does not compare the margin to the lease directly, and stop() releases only if isLeader() is true.
